chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Rayyan from al-Husayn ibn Rashid from some of his companions from Mis'mam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)
That the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade a man from closing his eyes during the prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on closing the eyes during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a specific etiquette (adab) for prayer, prohibiting men from closing their eyes (ghumad al-ayn) to avoid the distraction of sleep or excessive introspection, tracing the ruling from Imam Ali through Imam al-Sadiq to the Prophet. While some scholars view this as a recommended practice (mustahabb) rather than an absolute prohibition, it highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining full visual and mental presence (khushu) during worship. The chain underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition through the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the authority of Imam al-Sadiq in transmitting practical legal details.
